answer.answer: The complaint was made by [PERSON_1], who says she is the daughter of the account holder Mr [PERSON_2]. 432cfcad6980b166.question: Which policy rules decide this case, and what do they require the handler to do?

answer.answer: Key rules: CH-6 makes this High severity (vulnerable customer at risk of harm). VUL-1/VUL-4 require referral to Vulnerable Customer Support (dementia is a health driver; arrears and unaffordable payments show financial difficulty). ESC-1 routes arrears to Lending Specialists. LND-3 caps contact at one call a day and three a week; the log shows 23 calls in 1-14 Oct. LND-4/FEE-4 require review of arrears fees. VUL-6 matters: the note says the account was discussed with the daughter, but the file does not show any third-party mandate or power of attorney, so the handler must check authority before discussing the account further. Whether the customer was asked about support is not in the file. Outcome and redress are for an authorised person.

supporting_quotes.quote: her father has dementia and your collections team has been ringing him up to five times a day about his credit card arrears
Collections log shows 23 outbound calls 1-14 Oct.
a vulnerable customer at risk of harm

Cases with a vulnerability indicator *and* any of: financial difficulty, risk to health or wellbeing, suspected financial abuse, or bereavement must be referred to the Vulnerable Customer Support team.
Contact must not be excessive: no more than one call per day and three per week.
A lending decision, affordability, mortgage or loan arrears → *Lending Specialists*.
The bank may only discuss the account with a third party (such as a relative or carer) where there is a valid authority on file (third-party mandate or power of attorney).
Arrears fees must be reviewed where the customer was in financial difficulty (see FEE-4).
